title: (No AI) You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/04/STK255_Google_Gemini_B_474198.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code [directly within Google Gemini](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-app/edit-files-directly/). The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in the web version for now.

Google added support for [generating and downloading files](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/920870/now-google-gemini-will-create-spreadsheets-pdfs-and-other-files-if-you-ask) in Gemini earlier this year, but now you can tweak those files without leaving the Gemini app. Google says you can expand documents to edit them in full-screen mode and highlight text in files to ask Gemini questions or prompt …

title: (No AI) Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
author: Tom Warren
content:
![Vector illustration of the Microsoft logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25832912/STK095_MICROSOFT_2_CVirginia_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO **Satya Nadella** has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft's workforce. Microsoft is now offering voluntary buyouts [to around 60,000 employees](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1018666/microsoft-expands-buyouts-60000-employees-eligible) across the US, UK, Canada, and India.

It's the first time the company has presented such an offer to so many employees, expanding greatly upon the [retirement offer](https://www.theverge.com/news/917451/microsoft-voluntary-retirement-offer-rewards-bonus-stock-changes) that was limited to around 9,000 employees earlier this year. It's all part of an ongoing effort to avoid reducing investment in AI infrastructure by lowering Microsoft's operating cos …
